new URL('/one', 'http://example.com/').href    // 'http://example.com/one'
new URL('/two', 'http://example.com/one').href // 'http://example.com/two'
```

Note that `url.resolve` is now marked as deprecated in the [Node docs](https://nodejs.org/api/url.html#url_url_resolve_from_to).

As Andreas correctly points out in a comment, `url.resolve` (also [deprecated](https://nodejs.org/api/url.html#url_url_parse_urlstring_parsequerystring_slashesdenotehost)) would only help if the problem is as simple as the example.  `url.parse` also applies to this question because it returns consistently and predictably formatted fields via the `URL` object that reduces the need for "code full of ifs". However, `new URL()` is also the replacement for `url.parse`.
